```{r}
library(igraph) # only necessary for this exercise
library(DT) # only necessary for this exercise
source("setup.R")
```

#### Creating park "centroids"

When a park unit contains multiple locations like the Manhattan Project National Historic Park, centroid creation is inappropriate:

```{r}
parks <- getParkSystem()

mapr_centroid <- parks %>%
  filter(UNIT_CODE == "MAPR") %>%
  st_centroid()

mapr_boundary <- parks %>%
  filter(UNIT_CODE == "MAPR")

mapview(mapr_boundary, lwd = 15, col.region = "red", color = "red") + mapview(mapr_centroid)
```

So, we can "explode" any multipolygon into a single feature. But, some of these units get separated "too" much, see examples of Rocky Mountain and Acadia:

```{r}
# grab CONUS parks
units_poly <- getParkSystem() %>% 
  # remove non-CONUS
  filter(!is.na(STATE) & !STATE %in% c("AK", "HI", "PR", "AS", "GU", "MP", "VI"),
         # Dry Tortugas not often included in CONUS datasets (too far off the Florida mainland)
         UNIT_CODE != "DRTO") %>% 
  st_cast("POLYGON") %>% 
  st_transform(5070)   # convert to meters projection

# group by park and "split"
exploded <- units_poly %>% 
  dplyr::group_split(UNIT_CODE)

romo_boundary <- exploded %>%
  rbindlist() %>%
  filter(UNIT_CODE == "ROMO") %>%
  st_as_sf() %>%
  rowid_to_column() %>% mutate(rowid = as.character(rowid))

mapview(romo_boundary, zcol = "rowid")

acad_boundary <- exploded %>%
  rbindlist() %>% 
  filter(UNIT_CODE == "ACAD") %>%
  st_as_sf() %>%
  rowid_to_column() %>% mutate(rowid = as.character(rowid))

mapview(acad_boundary, zcol = "rowid")
```

Therefore, I "regroup" split boundaries that are within 15 km of each other (15km is arbitrary):

```{r}
#so, cluster polygons within 15 km
# clustered <- exploded %>% 
#   map_dfr(function(p) {
#     # find which same UNIT_CODE polygons are within 15km of each other:
#     nb <- sf::st_is_within_distance(p, p, dist = 15000)
#     # turn that into a graph and get connected components (AI suggestion):
#     g <- igraph::graph_from_adj_list(nb, mode = "all")
#     comp <- igraph::components(g)$membership
#     p$cluster_id <- comp
#     return(p)
#   })


clustered <- exploded %>%
  map_dfr(function(p) {
    # If a park only has 1 polygon, don't waste time on it
    if(nrow(p) <= 1) {
      p$cluster_id <- 1
      return(p)
    }
    
    # SPEED FIX: Use a simplified version of the geometry just for the distance check
    p_sim <- st_simplify(p, dTolerance = 5)
    
    nb <- sf::st_is_within_distance(p_sim, dist = 15000)
    
    g <- igraph::graph_from_adj_list(nb)
    p$cluster_id <- igraph::components(g)$membership
    return(p)
  })

# within each cluster (per park)
units_clustered <- clustered %>% 
  group_by(UNIT_CODE, cluster_id) %>% 
  summarize(do_union = TRUE, .groups = "drop") %>% 
  st_cast("MULTIPOLYGON") %>% 
  # st_transform(st_crs(getParkSystem())) %>%
  mutate(cluster_id = as.character(cluster_id))
```

Next, we explore how to grab appropriate point locations that are the best representation of these park units. Centroids are most obvious, but can be a location outside the park boundary. We could instead use st_point_on_surface(), which guarantees it falls within polygon boundary:

```{r}
centroids <- units_clustered %>%
  st_centroid() %>%
  filter(UNIT_CODE == "ROMO")

pseudo_centroids <- units_clustered %>%
  st_point_on_surface() %>%
  filter(UNIT_CODE == "ROMO")

mapview(pseudo_centroids, col.regions = "blue") + mapview(centroids, col.regions = "pink") +
  mapview(units_clustered %>% filter(UNIT_CODE == "ROMO"), layer.name = "ROMO")

centroids <- units_clustered %>%
  st_centroid() %>%
  filter(UNIT_CODE == "ACAD")

pseudo_centroids <- units_clustered %>%
  st_point_on_surface() %>%
  filter(UNIT_CODE == "ACAD")

mapview(pseudo_centroids, col.regions = "blue") + mapview(centroids, col.regions = "pink") +
  mapview(units_clustered %>% filter(UNIT_CODE == "ACAD"), zcol = "cluster_id", layer.name = "ACAD")

centroids <- units_clustered %>%
  st_centroid() %>%
  filter(UNIT_CODE == "NIOB")

pseudo_centroids <- units_clustered %>%
  st_point_on_surface() %>%
  filter(UNIT_CODE == "NIOB")

mapview(pseudo_centroids, col.regions = "blue") + mapview(centroids, col.regions = "pink") +
  mapview(units_clustered %>% filter(UNIT_CODE == "NIOB"), layer.name = "NIOB")

centroids <- units_clustered %>%
  st_centroid() %>%
  filter(UNIT_CODE == "OBRI")

pseudo_centroids <- units_clustered %>%
  st_point_on_surface() %>%
  filter(UNIT_CODE == "OBRI")

mapview(pseudo_centroids, col.regions = "blue") + mapview(centroids, col.regions = "pink") +
  mapview(units_clustered %>% filter(UNIT_CODE == "OBRI"), layer.name = "OBRI")
```

#### Comparing to CCRP centroids

It looks like they removed portions of park boundaries where their distances created a problem, like Manhattan Project, but the point also does not appear to be created from the "centroid" nor the "st_point_on_surface"... 🤔

```{r}
ccrp_centroids <- read_csv("data/CCRP_automated_climate_futures/spatial-data/centroid_county.csv") %>%
  st_as_sf(., coords = c("Lon", "Lat"), crs = 4326) 

mapview(ccrp_centroids %>% filter(UNIT_CODE == "MAPR"), layer.name = "CCRP", col.region = "brown") + 
  mapview(units_clustered %>% filter(UNIT_CODE == "MAPR") %>% st_point_on_surface(), layer.name = "CSU Pseudo-Centroid") +
  mapview(units_clustered %>% filter(UNIT_CODE == "MAPR") %>% st_centroid(), col.region = "magenta", layer.name = "CSU Centroid") +
  mapview(units_clustered %>% filter(UNIT_CODE == "MAPR"), zcol = "cluster_id", layer.name = "MAPR")

mapview(ccrp_centroids %>% filter(UNIT_CODE == "ACAD"), layer.name = "CCRP", col.region = "brown") + 
  mapview(units_clustered %>% filter(UNIT_CODE == "ACAD") %>% st_point_on_surface(), layer.name = "CSU Pseudo-Centroid") +
  mapview(units_clustered %>% filter(UNIT_CODE == "ACAD") %>% st_centroid(), col.region = "magenta", layer.name = "CSU Centroid") +
  mapview(units_clustered %>% filter(UNIT_CODE == "ACAD"), zcol = "cluster_id", layer.name = "ACAD")

mapview(ccrp_centroids %>% filter(UNIT_CODE == "THRO"), layer.name = "CCRP", col.region = "brown") + 
  mapview(units_clustered %>% filter(UNIT_CODE == "THRO") %>% st_point_on_surface(), layer.name = "CSU Pseudo-Centroid") +
  mapview(units_clustered %>% filter(UNIT_CODE == "THRO") %>% st_centroid(), col.region = "magenta", layer.name = "CSU Centroid") +
  mapview(units_clustered %>% filter(UNIT_CODE == "THRO"), zcol = "cluster_id", layer.name = "THRO")
```

Their CCRP park centroid layer is also missing some parks:

```{r}
missing_parks <- parks %>%
  filter(!UNIT_CODE %in% ccrp_centroids$UNIT_CODE) 

DT::datatable(missing_parks %>%
                distinct(UNIT_NAME, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
                select(UNIT_NAME, UNIT_CODE))
```
